notes: *rooted out of it* is divided with *out* on the verb and *of* on `מִן`, on the parallel of the first colon's *cut off from the land*, where the particle completes the phrasal verb and the preposition takes its own word (rule 44). The competing reading gives the whole *out of* to `מִן` headed on *out* under rule 24 and leaves the verb the bare *rooted*; the accepted division is named in that unit's note.
The impersonal active `יִסְּחוּ` is recast as an English passive, so its auxiliaries belong to the verb's unit (rule 17).
Both substantival plurals take the supplied *the* that makes them noun phrases (rule 46); the marginal *Or, earth* was read and set aside (rule 38).
